trigger: docs/ops-runbooks/quarantine-store-backfill-recovery.md's first-listed remedy for the 5000-row backfill sanity cap was pruning released records from the legacy SQLite file directly, before retrying the backfill
summary: Rows pruned via the runbook's documented remedy never reach Postgres, and the backfill fingerprints the reduced set as complete -- nothing later detects the loss. ADR-0047's own Follow-ups section states this history must never be deleted ('a REGRESSION for a SOC 2 security-containment control'); the runbook's own supported remedy directly contradicted the ADR it was written to accompany. Found by external PR review (Doomgoose, plus a parallel Kimi K3 + Codex pass), not by this branch's own governance run across 3 Gate 8 rounds + a Gate 2 light pass + a targeted C++ coverage-gap closure -- a real blind spot in this session's review coverage: doc-vs-ADR contradiction checking was not itself covered by any of those passes. reviewed_at_sha is a synthetic merge-test SHA from the reviewer's own tooling (dev merged into this branch for a throwaway compile+test worktree), not a commit in this branch's own history -- commit_range is unresolved accordingly.
classification_rationale: the runbook's remedy text contradicts ADR-0047's explicit, deliberate retention policy for the same data -- a doc actively wrong about a compliance-relevant invariant, not merely incomplete
